summary:
All 27 findings were checked against copy B (/home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/frozen/impl_unified_B). None is a default-off break. Every bug and plan mismatch is real and is fixed in the copy, each with a test that goes red when the defect is put back. The style and test-gap findings are fixed except the points under "left". With the four switches off the engine behaves as before: 118 of the 122 test files of the folder give the same summary line as before the fixes, and the other 4 differ only by the tests added.

Read first
- REPORT.md is not updated. A subagent may not write report files in this session (the refusal the engineer met), so the file on disk still describes the copy before the fixes. This output is its new content.
- Everything ran on CPU. Nothing ran on a GPU or with more than one rank. The two test files that run the real init_hicache still fail for want of a GPU, as before.
- The merge with copy A was only dry-run on scratch copies.

What the fixes change (switches on only)
- Retire and the heal no longer undo each other. The write of a page parked for retire heals nothing above it, so an explicit end without the write skip queues the last reply alone, not the chain just zeroed.
- Retire at the ack goes fragment by fragment. After a split, only the fragments the retire walk took are zeroed and left unstored; the rest get the normal verdict and no id stays parked.
- The heal walks the whole root path, so a hole above a stored node is rewritten too. A write below pages parked for retire takes them off the retire: something was built on them after the end.
- A cleared store also drops the queued operation ids and the parked pages. A detach clears every stored mark and both sets.
- An ended session's own leaves are known by the last page key of each turn it committed, so a reply read back from the SSD under a new node id is still retired.
- Only a turn that an exact (v1) hint named ends its session by carrying no next-turn action. A known session's turn that comes without a hint forgets the session's tail, with a new log reason: ntp_end explicit=0 why=no_hint.
- The write skip decides nothing while the store is detached. I found this while fixing: the ids of skipped nodes piled up, since no write came to spend them.
- The touch thread holds its backend weakly and survives a failing job; close() warns and drops the jobs left when the thread is still busy after 5 s.

Switches, all off by default, and what each needs
- SGLANG_HICACHE_STORAGE_TRACK_STORED (bool): the stored marks, the heal, the resets at clear and detach, stored= on h2s_done, h2s_short. Needs --hicache-host-memory-mode cache, the Python tree core and PP = 1 (new).
- SGLANG_HICACHE_NIXL_TOUCH_INTERVAL_S (seconds, 0 = off; the extra-config key touch_interval_s wins): the touch thread and the refresh at a request's match. Needs TRACK_STORED and a NIXL file backend that writes files on this rank.
- SGLANG_HICACHE_STORAGE_SKIP_ENDED_WRITES (bool): no SSD write for a turn whose hint ends its session (h2s_skip), and the registration that follows the explicit end (ntp_end). Needs TRACK_STORED and the next-turn prefetcher.
- SGLANG_HICACHE_NIXL_RETIRE_ENDED_PAGES (bool; the key retire_ended_pages wins): mtime zero for an ended session's own pages (l3_retire, l3_retire_ack), and the same registration. Needs TRACK_STORED, the prefetcher, the touch interval above 0 (new), a FULL-only cache without sidecar pools (now checked again when a pool is registered after init) and a NIXL file backend.
- A switch that lacks what it needs stays off and logs "HiCache retention: <name> stays off: it needs ...".

Deviations from the plan added by the fixes
- Two dependencies. TRACK_STORED needs PP = 1: the stored verdict is a minimum over TP ranks only, and the PP sync hands down PP rank 0's. Retire needs the touch interval: a retired page read back counts as stored, and only the refresh gives its files a recent mtime again.
- The heal covers the whole root path, not the unstored run right above the node, and is skipped for a write parked for retire.
- A detach clears every stored mark, where the plan only unmarks the dropped operations: the next store attached may be another one. After a detach and re-attach of the same store, the first write under each chain rewrites that chain (a stat and a utime per file with skip-stored writes on).
- Own leaves are told by last page key. The plan used "not registered", the engineer node ids.
- The refresh rule is kept as built and its bound restated. A request's match refreshes every stored node of its chain once any of them is an interval old or was read back from the SSD. So a page is touched once per interval per chain through it, plus once for each read that lands below it. The threads reviewer estimates about 6.3 M utime calls at campaign 34's ec_full volume against the 1.72 M of the plan's count, at 2.8 us a call on a temp directory; the journal load on the SSD volume is unmeasured.
- ntp_end has one more reason value, no_hint. l3_retire_ack pages= counts the retired fragments' pages.

First campaign arm
- Set SGLANG_HICACHE_STORAGE_TRACK_STORED=1 SGLANG_HICACHE_NIXL_TOUCH_INTERVAL_S=300 SGLANG_HICACHE_NIXL_RETIRE_ENDED_PAGES=1 SGLANG_HICACHE_STORAGE_SKIP_ENDED_WRITES=1, against the same arm with all four unset, and run past the first cleaner pass (minute 87.5 to 88.3 at campaign 34's setting).
- It needs what the hinted arms have: the prefetcher on, host memory mode cache, write-through, the NIXL file backend, TP = PP = 1, a FULL-only model, and hints that state the end.
- The start-up line must read "HiCache retention: track_stored=1 skip_ended_writes=1 touch_interval_s=300 retire_ended_pages=1", with no "stays off" warning.
- Retire alone is now refused. To isolate the refresh, set TRACK_STORED and the touch interval only (no hints needed). To run retire without the periodic refresh, set a very large interval: only pages read back are then touched.
- What to read: h2s_skip tokens (4.7 to 4.8 % of inserted tokens by the plan; 0.7 % means only replies are skipped); ntp_end explicit=1 (566 sessions in ec_full) against explicit=0 by reason; l3_retire with pages above 0 (count the pages=0 lines); l3_retire_ack; l3_touch files= per second (expect several times the plan's 239); stored=0 and h2s_short (none expected). The effect to look for: after each "NIXL L3 cleanup", fewer s2h_query storage_hit=0 on returning turns and fewer "failed to retrieve page".

Merge notes (dry run at about 8:30 PM ET on 2026-11-26, git merge-file -p on scratch copies over frozen/impl_unified_base)
- Against copy A: no conflict in the four engine files both copies change (environ.py, next_turn_prefetch.py, unified_tree_core.py, unified_radix_cache.py), nor in test_next_turn_prefetch.py and test_storage_read_dispatch.py. The merged engine files parse; they were not run. There are two conflicts in the import block of test_next_use_eviction.py, where both copies add imports and A extends the components import: a union keeps that import twice.
- Against the working tree (the load hold, keep_touched in the cleaner): environ.py and test_hicache_nixl_cleaner.py merge without conflict.

fixed: Correctness 1 and threads 1 (bug), the heal undid the retire when the write skip was off: real. The last reply's write, parked for retire, ran the heal and re-queued the chain just zeroed. Fix: write_backup_storage runs no heal for a node parked for retire. Test: test_next_use_eviction.py TestStoredMarksOnACpuTree::test_the_last_replys_write_does_not_bring_a_retired_chain_back, on the real CPU tree through the host-copy ack and the write ack, with the write skip off and on.

Correctness 2 (bug), retire at the ack hit the whole operation after a split: real. Fix: UnifiedTreeCore.finish_storage_write decides per fragment. Only the fragments the retire walk parked are zeroed and left unstored, the others get the normal verdict, and every parked id of the operation is dropped. Test: test_a_node_retired_while_its_write_is_queued_is_retired_at_the_ack, moved from the stub tree to the real tree, with a split with and without another session's branch.

Correctness 3 (bug), the heal stopped at the first stored ancestor: real. Fix: unstored_ancestors walks the whole root path, up to the first ancestor without a host copy. A write below pages parked for retire also takes them off the retire. Tests: test_a_child_write_first_rewrites_an_unstored_ancestor (a short ack followed by a full one leaves the hole above a stored node) and test_a_write_below_a_retired_chain_brings_it_back.

Correctness 4 (bug), retire granted without the refresh: real. Fix: resolve_retention_switches grants the retire only with a touch interval above 0 and logs the refusal. Test: test_storage_read_dispatch.py TestRetentionSwitches::test_a_switch_missing_what_it_needs_stays_off_and_says_so.

Correctness 5 (bug), a turn a table named counted as an explicit end when it came with no hint: real. Fix: only a turn named by an exact (v1) hint ends by carrying no action; the name recorded for the next rid carries that mark. A known session's turn without a hint forgets the tail and logs ntp_end explicit=0 why=no_hint. Tests: TestPlanRegistration::test_an_exact_hint_session_ends_at_the_turn_with_no_next (table-named case added) and TestDeadlineMode::test_a_turn_with_no_usable_entry_is_ranked_as_un_hinted_not_as_ended.

Correctness 6 (bug), a clear left the queued operation id on its node: real. Fix: clear_storage_marks also resets storage_write_op, and the set of pages parked for retire is emptied. Test: the clear case of test_clearing_or_detaching_the_store_clears_every_mark (a write queued before the clear and acked after it stays unstored).

Correctness 7 (test gap), the retire tests stopped at the retire call: real. The tests of the six items above run on the real CPU tree and ack through the cache's own drain (the host copy, then the write), including a split between submit and retire, a turn after the end while a retired write is queued, and a short ack followed by a full one.

Correctness 8 (nit), a detach kept the stored marks and both sets: real. Fix: a detach clears every stored mark, the queued ids and both sets (StorageAttachment._release_pending_storage_ops calls UnifiedRadixCache._forget_storage_copies). Test: the detach case of test_clearing_or_detaching_the_store_clears_every_mark.

Correctness 9 and threads 2 (nit, plan mismatch), the claim that a page is touched at most once per interval: real. The bound is per chain. The docstring of _refresh_served_chain, a comment in test_a_stale_tail_takes_its_fresh_head_along_and_a_second_match_takes_nothing and this report now say so. The rule itself is kept (see rejected).

Test: test_hicache_nixl_storage.py TestNixlTouch::test_a_touch_that_fails_does_not_end_the_thread (first job raises, second is applied, the warning is logged, no thread after close), with a mutation for it.

Rules 11 (nit), small contracts unpinned: real, four of five pinned. The ntp_end fields at the exact-hint end; tokens= of h2s_skip and at_ack= of l3_retire on a node of two pages; the bound of the per-session records (test_what_is_kept_per_session_for_its_end_is_bounded_oldest_first).

Found while fixing, not in the findings: with the store detached, the write skip kept flagging ended turns, and their node ids piled up because no write came to spend them. _turn_ends_session now decides nothing while storage is off; the prompt-insert test covers it.
rejected: Correctness 9, the cut 'touch from the head down to the deepest stale node only (the plan's rule)': not taken. It makes more calls, not fewer: each time a deeper node turns stale the whole prefix above it is touched again, whereas the present rule stamps the chain together so its next refresh is one interval away.

Threads 2, the cut 'stamp a stale tail just below its nearest fresh ancestor': not taken here. It needs a wall-clock stamp per node and changes the design; it is listed under left as an open decision.
Correctness 1 and threads 1, the interim 'make the resolver refuse retire without the write skip': not needed once the bug is fixed; retire without the write skip is tested.
Threads 4, the alternative of a minimum over the PP group: not taken. It needs a new collective on the PP group that cannot be tested here; the switch is refused with PP above 1 instead.

Threads 7, 'a stop flag so that close() discards queued jobs': only after the join times out. close() still does the jobs queued before it, because the detach path and the tests rely on a retire queued just before close being done.
Rules 11, the reset of the two id sets in _reset_full: no test added. Node ids are never reused (a class-level counter), so a stale id cannot match a node of the rebuilt tree.
Rules 9, the class default `retention` between two methods: left where it is until the merge, since copy A adds attributes at the class header.

Refresh cost, open decision: each read that lands below a chain touches the whole in-memory chain again. l3_touch files= per second in the first arm is the number to read. Two ways to cut it, neither built: stamp read-back pages just below their head's last stamp (needs a wall-clock stamp per node), or touch only the stale nodes and accept a tail newer than its head for up to one interval, as freshly written pages already are.
Retire without the write skip writes the last turn and then zeroes it at the ack: correct but wasteful. Whether the retire alone should also skip those writes is the author's call.
A store that fails every write: each write retries its whole unstored root path, so the write queue grows with the chain depth. This is the plan's heal; h2s_short counts show it. No bound was added.

A retire's zeroing still queued on the touch thread when a fork's rewrite of the same pages lands leaves them at mtime zero until their next refresh. It needs a fork within the touch backlog, which is milliseconds at campaign 34's volume; not closed.
Race X3 (a touch that lands after the cleaner's scan does not save the page) is unchanged, and the utime cost on cold inodes of the SSD volume is still unmeasured.

Retire limits that remain: the walk stops at a reply left by an aborted turn; an own reply under a node where another session branches is left (for example the first reply when another session shares the whole first prompt); a session seen for one turn is not retired.

R1 limits as in the engineer's report: a one-request session that ends explicitly does not get its first prompt written until a session that does not end extends it; under write_back the skip does nothing.
Open decision from the plan: a request with no next-turn action that no earlier turn named (a client that sends no hints) is still registered as ended at commit.
The prefetcher's two end switches are fixed when it is created; a storage backend attached at runtime with another setting changes the cache, not the prefetcher.
HiCacheNixl's own condition is tested for an MLA rank that writes no files; the object-store plugin branch needs an object store and is untested.
Steps 4 to 6 (P1, P2, R5, R2, X3, X5) are not started, as assigned. The marks they read are still node.storage_stored and node.storage_write_op.
